newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down, central bank buys dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down, central bank buys dlrs.

text.p: The Philippine peso fell to the day's low of 26.246 at the close on Wednesday from 26.242 after the Central Bank bought dollars in late trading, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.245 to the dollar versus the previous 26.239. Volume narrowed to $102.20 million from $144.35 million.
"The Central Bank was replenishing its reserves after selling dollars last week," a local bank dealer said.
The peso opened weak as some banks tried to buy up the dollar, knowing that the Central Bank had stepped in to buy dollars at 26.24 pesos on Tuesday.
But inflows for direct and equity investments eventually strengthened the peso, traders said.
In the afternoon, the market saw Central Bank purchasing dollars at a higher rate of 26.245 pesos, weakening the peso in late trade, they said.
One dealer estimated the Central Bank bought about $15 to $18 million.
